modelDescription: A linear price model whose L2 penalty limits large coefficients.
intuition: Ridge combines the features using learned weights. Its alpha penalty discourages very large weights, which can stabilize predictions when engine size and power are correlated.
parameters: alpha controls the penalty on large coefficients. Compare the default alpha of 1 with 10.
limitations: A straight-line relationship may miss interactions and nonlinear depreciation. Coefficient size depends on feature scaling, so it is not a universal feature-importance ranking.

modelDescription: A sequence of small trees, each learning corrections to the current predictions.
intuition: With squared-error loss, the next tree learns residual errors from the ensemble so far. The learning rate controls how much of that correction is added.
parameters: Compare the default 100 trees and learning rate 0.1 with 200 trees and learning rate 0.05. More, smaller corrections may improve the fit.
limitations: Deep trees or too many aggressive corrections can overfit. Trees are sequential, so this search can take longer. Large-price errors can still dominate RMSE.

modelDescription: Many bootstrap-trained trees whose predictions are averaged.
intuition: Each tree learns from a bootstrap sample of training rows. Averaging their predictions usually reduces variance compared with one tree. Feature subsampling is controlled by max_features; the default regressor considers all features.
parameters: Compare unrestricted default trees with depth 12 and at least 3 rows per leaf. These limits can reduce overfitting.
limitations: Averaging reduces variance but does not eliminate overfitting. Forests can be slower and less interpretable than one tree. Regression impurity importance is not Gini importance or a causal explanation.

modelDescription: A set of feature-threshold rules ending in numerical predictions.
intuition: The tree chooses splits that reduce squared error within the child groups. A leaf predicts the mean training target of its rows. If the target is log price, that mean is on the log scale until we reverse it.
parameters: Compare the unrestricted default tree with a depth limit of 8 and at least 5 rows per leaf. A restricted tree may generalize better.
limitations: An unrestricted tree can overfit and change substantially when training rows change. A shallow tree may underfit. A single split is an association, not evidence of causation.

modelDescription: A nonlinear regression function with a tolerance for small errors.
intuition: SVR fits a function with an epsilon-wide tolerance around it. Errors outside that tolerance are penalized. The RBF kernel represents nonlinear similarity between cars.
parameters: Compare the default C of 1 with 10. C controls the penalty for errors outside the epsilon tolerance. epsilon stays at 0.1 and has different meaning on the price and log-price scales.
limitations: SVR is sensitive to feature scales and settings. We use the same five scaled numeric columns as Assignment 1; ownership and seats retain their original units. This scaling choice is a limitation to discuss, not an excuse to tune on the hold-out.

modelDescription: Predicts from the targets of the most similar training cars.
intuition: KNN stores the training cars. At prediction time it finds nearby cars in feature space and averages their targets. Distance weighting gives nearer cars more influence.
parameters: Compare the default 5 equally weighted neighbours with 9 neighbours weighted by distance. Nearby cars then have more influence.
limitations: Small K can follow noise; large K can smooth away useful local differences. Distances depend on scaling and feature choice. We retain Assignment 1’s five scaled columns, with seats and ownership in their original units.
